findings.claim: Checklist item paired_population is green: 'Every arm scored on identical events — 4813 events in the shared window; every arm has seen all of them'.
findings.problem: Having seen an event is not the same as having scored one. The arms report different screen samples on that shared stream: control, placebo, hold-12h, tp-7pct all at screen_n=1550, sl-5pct at 1549, vol-4x at 866, entry-8pct at 496. Any arm-vs-control comparison for vol-4x or entry-8pct is therefore run on a strict subset of control's population, which is population mismatch (PM), not a paired test. The green detail establishes shared detection, not shared scoring, so the checkbox does not establish its own title.

findings.claim: entry-8pct screen_dWR=0.0pp and vol-4x screen_dWR=0.0pp are reported alongside screen_wr=51.613 (n=496) and screen_wr=51.27 (n=866) against control screen_wr=49.935 (n=1550).
findings.problem: These two arms report a win-rate delta of exactly zero while their stated win rates differ from control's on the same table. Either dWR is not being computed for arms whose population is reduced, or it is stale — in both cases the field silently reads like 'no effect' for the two arms that most need a delta, and it is identical to the placebo's legitimately-zero 0.0pp. A reader cannot distinguish 'measured no difference' from 'never measured' in the arena table.

findings.claim: entry_granularity_declared is marked ok with the assurance that 'Arm-vs-arm comparisons stay valid — all arms share this kernel' despite the kernel reading pumps +0.59pp larger on average across 200 matched setups.
findings.problem: That assurance holds only for arms whose changed parameter is orthogonal to the mis-measured quantity. entry-8pct changes pump_pct to 8.0 — the very quantity the kernel systematically overstates by 0.59pp. A uniform upward pump bias moves the 8.0 threshold's admitted population, which is consistent with entry-8pct scoring only screen_n=496 against control's 1550. The shared-kernel argument does not neutralise a bias in the arm's own cut variable, so this non-critical 'declared' item is being used to wave through a comparison it does not cover.

findings.claim: backfill_cannot_promote is green and critical: 'Only live-tape evidence can promote — 0 surfaced arm(s); none promoted from a screen'.
findings.problem: The gate is green because nothing has ever reached it, not because it was exercised and held. Meanwhile every headline number attached to every running arm (screen_wr, screen_ev, screen_dWR, screen_n around 1550) comes from the backfill tier of 4764 events, whereas the live tier holds 49 events and per-arm live_n is 3 to 13 against a planned confirm n=600. The arena display is therefore entirely backfill-driven while the checkbox implies live-only evidence discipline; a zero-denominator pass is not evidence the rule works.

findings.claim: Statistical reality states 'measured ghost arrival = 25.2 control trades/day', and arms_running is green with '5 running: tp-7pct, hold-12h, entry-8pct, sl-5pct, vol-4x'.
findings.problem: Two inconsistencies sit in the same context. First, the graveyard entry L-dedup-0h states the baseline as 25.6 control trades/day while the statistical-reality block states 25.2 — the same measured quantity is quoted at two values with no n attached to either. Second, control's live_n is 13 and the live tier holds 49 events total, which cannot be reconciled with an arrival of 25.2 or 25.6 control trades per day over a 62.0-day span; the arrival figure used to plan the confirm sample is not the rate the live tape is actually producing. entry-8pct in particular sits at live_n=3 with declined=46 and is still listed simply as 'running'.

findings.claim: sl-5pct is the leading arm, carrying screen_dWR=5.29pp on screen_n=1549.
findings.problem: The objective is win rate AND EV per trade, and on the same screen table sl-5pct posts screen_ev=0.029 against control's screen_ev=0.034 — it is behind control on the EV half of the objective while leading by 5.29pp on the win-rate half. The arena presents the win-rate delta as the arm's headline and never pairs it with an EV delta, which is the same one-sided framing the project already killed in G-08 and G-17 (a WR dial that does not lift net EV). No EV delta versus control on the same window is reported for any arm.
